summary.name: Vim
summary.one_liner: Vim is a highly configurable, long-established text editor (the "vi" included with most UNIX systems and Apple OS X) for efficiently creating and changing any kind of text.
use_cases: searching and replacing text across files
comparing file differences in diff mode
summary.what_it_does: Vim is a highly configurable text editor for creating and changing any kind of text efficiently. Its listed features include a persistent multi-level undo tree, an extensive plugin system, support for hundreds of programming languages and file formats, powerful search and replace, and integration with many tools. The page reports Vim 9.2 with Vim9 scripting enhancements (enums, generic functions, tuples), an improved diff mode, and new completion features. A GTK 4 GUI backend is available as an opt-in build option on X11 and Wayland. The page also links to a plugin repository with thousands of scripts.
notable: Extensive plugin system with a public script repository (6,020 scripts listed)
Vim 9.2 with Vim9 scripting enhancements and improved diff mode
Opt-in GTK 4 GUI backend enabled with --enable-gui=gtk4
caveats: The GTK 4 backend is opt-in for now while it stabilises; GTK 3 remains the default build option
Vim homepage was read-only during a hosting migration, so plugin updates were not possible at that time
